div.l: The fore he songe so meryly and loude.
Now have y tolde yow soothely in a clause
Testate tharray the nombre and eke the cause
Whi that assembled was this compaignye
Īn South werke at this gentyl hostelrye.
That hight the tabard fast by sydes the belle
But now is tyme to yow for to telle
How that we beren vs that ilke nyght
Whan wee were in that hostelry a lyght
And aftyr wol y telle of our͗e viage
And al the remenant of our͗e pilgⁱrimage
But first y pᵃray yow of youre curtesye
That ye ne Recte it noght my vilenye
Theigh that y pleynly speke in this matere
To telle yow of her wordes and her chere
Ne theigh y speke hir wordes ꝓproperly
For this ye knowen also wel as .y.
Who so telleth a tale after aman
He moste reherce as nygh as eủer he can.
Eủery worde yif it be in his charge
Al speke he neủer so rudely ne so large.
Or elles moste he tellen his tale vntrewe
Or feyne thynges or fynde wordes newe.
He may not spare al theigh he were his brother
He moste as wel say on word as an nother
Criste spak him selfe ful brode in holy wryt
And wel ye witte no vilenye is hit.
Yit plato seyth who so kan him rede
The word moste be cosyn to the dede
Also y pᵃray yow to foryeue it me
Al haue y noght sette folke in her degre.
Here in this tale as that thei sholden stonde
My wit is short ye may wel vnderstonde
¶ Gret chere maad oure hoste eủerychone
And to the soper sette he vs a noon
He s̉erued vs wyth vitaille of the best
Strong was the wyne and wel to drynke vs lest
A semely man oure host. was wythalle
For to ben a marchal in an halle
A large man he was wyth eyen steepe
